title.narrative: Strengthened labour administration system for more effective labour market governance, improved working conditions and compliance

description.narrative: Labour inspection is a key element of any labour administration system for enduring the implementation of labour policies, providing feedback and allowing for a readjustment of these policies as necessary. In recent years, the importance of labour inspection in promoting decent work has been widely recognized. The ILO through this Country Programme Outcome is working to strengthen the labour inspection systems in Malawi with a view to ensuring labour law compliance through the promotion of relevant international labour standards, and technical advisory services and projects. Labour Law Reforms: With the support of the ILO, Malawi carrying out a labour law reform process. The process has scored some success, notably with the Employment Policy. The revised Act defined employment relationships which were not clearly defined in the past and these included casual employment, fixed term contracts, seasonal employment, short-term contracts, temporal employment and part-time work. Strengthening Social Dialogue: To promote stable and harmonious industrial relations, government intends to strengthen social dialogue mechanisms. ILO undertook a study on the review of the Tripartite Labour Advisory Council (TLAC) which identified institutional deficiencies in the TLAC and capacity constraints for members of the TLAC and limited ability of labour administration to support social dialogue processes. Beneficiaries of interventions under this CPO include the workers of Malawi, Employers and the Government of Malawi especially the Inspectorate department under the Ministry of Labour and Social Security. Partners involved under the interventions include the Government of Malawi mainly through the Ministry of Labour and Social Security, Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security.
